_README: Web-sourced (named-outlet) facts used in the 2026-10-15 brief (covering Wednesday 2026-10-14's close), recorded per CLAUDE.md §14 so every attribution in prose traces to a file. Method: a first research pass (six topic researchers) gathered candidate items, but it exhausted the session's shared 200-search budget, so its fact-check stage could not re-search and returned mostly 'unconfirmed'. A second, independent verification pass (new budget, capped per agent) re-searched every item the brief cites; its verdicts, evidence, URLs and safe wording are the 'items' below, and the brief's wording follows each item's safe_wording. Article pages could not be opened in this sandbox (WebFetch DNS failures, proxy 403), so evidence is search-result titles, URLs and snippets showing outlet, date and wording. Where press numbers conflict with the state file, the state file wins (§4C): closes and percentage moves come from data/macro_series.csv, data/raw/movers_2026-10-14.json and data/raw/claims_check_2026-10-15.json. Item ids: P = press framing, M = macro/Fed data, V = movers, T = Tier 3 AI financing, C = claims context.

items.evidence: The AP headline is confirmed on syndicated copies dated 2026-10-14 (local10.com/news/2026/10/14/..., krcgtv.com, nvdaily.com). The nvdaily slug reads 'drop-toward', an earlier intraday version. A snippet quotes the AP text exactly: 'The S&P 500 fell 1.1% Wednesday for its fifth loss in the six days since setting its all-time high.' Snippets say AI names were the biggest drag (Dell -11.3%, Oracle -8.8%, Marvell -8.7%, chip index -4.3%). The exact phrase 'AI-industry stocks led the way lower' was not found. The Stan Choe byline was not seen on any 10-14 copy. apnews.com is blocked to search.
items.safe_wording: AP led with "US stocks drop to their worst day since July as inflation worsens," noting the S&P 500's 1.1% fall was "its fifth loss in the six days since setting its all-time high," with AI-related stocks among the biggest drags. Attribute to AP, not to a named byline.

items.evidence: The CNBC URL cnbc.com/2026/10/14/dell-stock-barclays-enterprise-ai.html carries the exact headline: "Dell stock plunges 11%, leading data center sell-off as fears mount about 'enterprise AI timing'". Several outlets (Yahoo Finance, Stocktwits, tradersagency, foreignpolicyjournal 2026/10/15) say Barclays analyst Tim Long cut Dell, HPE and NetApp to Equal Weight from Overweight on Oct 14, 2026. The quoted rationale is "we don't see a meaningful AI inflection yet": recent revenue strength reflects memory-price pass-through, not enterprise AI demand. items.safe_wording: CNBC reported Dell fell about 11% on Wednesday, leading a data-center hardware sell-off, after Barclays downgraded Dell, HPE and NetApp to equal weight (its neutral rating) from overweight. Barclays said it does not yet see a meaningful enterprise-AI inflection and that recent revenue strength reflects higher memory prices.

items.evidence: Benzinga's 'Oracle Stock Tumbles: What's Going On?' (URL benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/10/62358714) says Oracle fell Wednesday, reversing Tuesday's gains, amid uncertainty over approval of the gas pipeline for Project Jupiter in New Mexico. It says Oracle 'sent a letter to FERC asking for a fast ruling'. Bloomberg (bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-13/oracle-asks-regulators-to-expedite-gas-pipeline-for-data-center) confirms the letter, dated Oct 13, 2026. It was signed by Oracle SVP Josh Pitcock, who wrote 'Time remains of the essence'. The pipeline is the 17.8-mile Green Chile line, operated by an Energy Transfer subsidiary, now targeting February 2027. CAVEAT: Oracle closed down about 8.8% at $130.55, and other outlets attribute the drop differently. Motley Fool/Yahoo lead with 'Oracle Tumbles on Hotter CPI Data Lifting Treasury Yields'. CNBC and SiliconANGLE frame it as contagion from CoreWeave and AI-debt concerns. The pipeline is one stated reason among several, not the only one.
items.safe_wording: Oracle fell about 9%. Benzinga tied the move to approval uncertainty for the gas pipeline serving its Project Jupiter data center in New Mexico: in an Oct. 13 letter, reported by Bloomberg, Oracle asked FERC for a fast ruling. Other outlets attributed the drop to the hot CPI print and to AI-debt contagion from CoreWeave. Present it as several reported reasons, not a single cause.

items.evidence: The CNBC URL cnbc.com/2026/10/14/bank-of-america-bac-q3-2026-earnings.html carries the exact headline. The AMP version reads 'Bank of America shares drop 8% after...', where 8% was the early-trading move. Q3 revenue missed by about $570M, mostly on trading. Regulators fined the bank $1.2B late Tuesday over anti-money-laundering failures; Treasury said it failed to report more than $5B in suspicious transactions. Reported EPS was $0.91, or $1.08 adjusted. Motley Fool reports BAC closed at $51.39, down 4.76%, after being down nearly 10% early. Reuters' later edition had BAC down 5.3%.
items.safe_wording: CNBC: Bank of America shares dropped after a third-quarter revenue miss and a $1.2 billion regulatory penalty over anti-money-laundering failures. Use the script-verified close (roughly -5%), not the 8% early-trading figure in one CNBC headline version.

items.evidence: The Fox Business headline is exact: 'Skydance stock sinks 22% after company distributes nearly 471M warrants'. Variety (variety.com/2026/biz/news/...1236911580) ran 'Skydance Shares Skid Down 22% After Company Issues 471 Million Stock Warrants to Paramount Investors'. The stock closed down 22.2% at $7.06 on Oct 14. Other measures: Motley Fool says -23.84%; TipRanks and TheWrap cite 25% (intraday). Deadline framed it as 'Skydance Stock Tumbles In Technical Adjustment'. TICKER: Yes, SKYD is the former Paramount Skydance (PSKY). After the WBD acquisition closed Oct 6, 2026, the company was renamed Skydance, moved from Nasdaq to NYSE and changed its Class B ticker from PSKY to SKYD (NBC News, CNBC 10-06, SEC 8-K). Holders of record on Oct 5 received 470,746,773 warrants with a $12 strike, trading as SKYD WS from Oct 13; the warrants closed at $2.20 that day. NYSE ADJUSTMENT: Yes, but small. The NYSE cut the Oct 13 official close by $0.19368, from about $9.27 to about $9.07, using the $2.20 warrant close pro-rated to the roughly 471M of about 5B shares (about 9%) entitled to warrants. This comes from the Skydance press release, the SEC FWP and Yahoo. The ~22% drop is therefore measured from the already-adjusted $9.07 reference. The adjustment accounts for only about 2 points of it.
items.safe_wording: Skydance (SKYD, the former Paramount Skydance/PSKY, renamed after the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed Oct. 6) fell about 22% after distributing nearly 471 million warrants ($12 strike) to some Class B holders. Fox Business and Variety reported the drop. The NYSE adjusted the prior close down only about $0.19, to about $9.07, because only about 9% of shares received warrants, so the drop is measured after that adjustment. Do not call it purely technical without that caveat; Deadline called it a 'technical adjustment'.

items.evidence: Investing.com has transcript-article titles 'Earnings call transcript: Morgan Stanley beats Q3 2026 estimates, shares fall' and 'Earnings call transcript: State Street tops Q3 2026 EPS view but shares fall'. Morgan Stanley reported EPS of $3.03 vs $2.91 (LSEG) and revenue of $20.34B; the stock fell about 2.9% premarket. CNBC's Morgan Stanley story is dated 2026/10/14. State Street reported adjusted EPS of $3.69 vs $3.67, but revenue of about $4.0B missed the roughly $4.03B consensus. Its shares fell about 6.5-7.8% in reports. Benzinga's State Street piece is in its 26/10 URL path. The State Street day is October 2026; Oct 14 is not stated explicitly in what I saw, but is consistent with it.
items.safe_wording: Investing.com: Morgan Stanley beat Q3 estimates (EPS $3.03 vs $2.91) but shares fell. State Street topped the EPS view ($3.69 vs $3.67), but revenue slightly missed and shares fell. Use script-verified closing moves.

items.evidence: The Reuters midday headline 'Wall St slides as hot CPI data fuels rate-hike bets; chips, banks weigh' is confirmed via TradingView (reuters.com,2026:newsml_L6N4600XE) and Investing.com. Search summaries of that piece put consumer staples up 0.9% and healthcare up 1.7% midday. Closing figures from Xinhua and other wraps: Health Care +2.44% and Consumer Staples +2.21-2.38%, two of only three S&P sectors higher. REASON: I found no named major outlet (Reuters, AP, CNBC, Bloomberg, WSJ) explicitly explaining the outperformance. A search summary implied that Xinhua (english.news.cn, 2026-10-15) described a rotation into defensive names, but I could not verify that wording. Smaller sites (ts2.tech 'Defensives Lead', tradersagency) use 'defensives' framing. Company-specific items exist: MarketBeat ties Bristol-Myers' ~4% gain to positive Phase 3 results, and TradingKey ties Merck's gain to ESMO late-breaker news. Large drugmakers led (AZN, MRK, BMY, ABBV, LLY, PFE each up about 3.9-4.3% midday per TheStreet).
items.safe_wording: Health care and consumer staples rose while the S&P 500 fell (Reuters midday: health care +1.7%, staples +0.9%). Report the move as mechanical fact only. No major outlet stated a reason, so do not attribute one. If needed, logged as a hypothesis: 'defensive rotation on rate-hike bets', with a test.

items.evidence: TipRanks: 'T-Mobile Stock (TMUS) Rises as Raymond James Upgrades to Buy, Calls SpaceX Competition Fears "Overblown"'. The formal rating per Investing.com, Seeking Alpha and others is Outperform from Market Perform, with a $170 target, by analyst Frank Louthan on Oct 12, 2026. Louthan called the fears 'overblown, as they are 3+ years away'. The upgrade followed a 13.3% TMUS plunge on Friday Oct 9 after SpaceX agreed to buy spectrum from Grain Management. CNBC 'The SpaceX threat to telecom is real. How it could play out' is confirmed at cnbc.com/2026/10/13/spacex-wireless-telecom-threat.html; it cites a Pivotal Research estimate that Starlink could take up to 13% of the US wireless market over ten years. I found no T-Mobile-specific news dated Oct 14. Q3 earnings are due Oct 28.
items.safe_wording: T-Mobile has rebounded since Raymond James upgraded it on Oct. 12 (to Outperform, which TipRanks reported as 'Buy'), calling SpaceX competition fears 'overblown'. CNBC on Oct. 13 argued the SpaceX threat to telecom is real. I found no new T-Mobile-specific news on Oct. 14.

items.evidence: The CNBC URL cnbc.com/2026/10/14/coreweave-stock-bond-yields-ai-debt.html appears with the title 'CoreWeave stock sinks as bond yields surge near 15%' and, in another listing, 'CoreWeave shares tumble as bond yields near 15% on concern about AI borrowing binge'. items.safe_wording: CNBC: CoreWeave stock sank (about 15%) as yields on its bonds neared 15%, citing a 14.8% yield to maturity on its 9.625% 2032 notes. Drop the 'citing Bloomberg' attribution, or attribute separately: 'Bloomberg reported the 2032 notes below 80 cents on the dollar'.

items.evidence: The Reuters story 'Cost of AI default insurance spikes as data centre confidence wobbles' is dated Oct 15, 2026. Evidence for the date: the TradingView ID reuters.com,2026:newsml_L1N46104Z; the syndicated copy at 933thedrive.com/2026/10/15/...; Investing.com ('By Reuters', ID 4950549); AOL; and The Standard HK. items.evidence: The CNBC URL cnbc.com/2026/10/12/intel-broadcom-ceos-warn-capital-crunch-could-become-ai-bottleneck.html carries the exact headline. The remarks were made at the DBS Asia Future Forward conference in Singapore. Broadcom's Hock Tan said financing could become a bigger obstacle than chip, memory or power shortages. Intel's Lip-Bu Tan said: 'If there's any challenge in the front, it's capital and the cost of capital... people want to see the ROI.' Benzinga, Quartz and Inc. corroborate.
items.safe_wording: CNBC (Oct. 12): the Intel and Broadcom CEOs warned that capital and the cost of capital could become the AI buildout's biggest bottleneck, ahead of chip or power shortages.

items.evidence: Bloomberg URL bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-15/blue-owl-s-stack-eyes-6-billion-loan-as-selloff-hits-ai-sector, title 'Stack Infrastructure Seeks $6 Billion Loan as AI Debt Concerns Grow'. Stack, owned by Blue Owl, is seeking an A$8.6B (about US$6B) five-year loan for its Melbourne data center project. It mandated lead arrangers this week, per a person familiar. Bloomberg framed the deal as a test of investor sentiment toward AI debt. CONTEXT: Bloomberg reported a similar A$8.5B (US$5.9B) Stack Melbourne loan on 2026-07-30, so this is a mandate milestone for a known financing, not a new or closed deal.
items.safe_wording: Bloomberg (Oct. 15): Blue Owl's Stack Infrastructure is seeking about A$8.6 billion (~US$6 billion) in a five-year loan for a Melbourne data center and has mandated arrangers. The loan is not yet closed. Bloomberg first reported it in July.

items.evidence: IN WINDOW: (1) Semafor exclusive, Oct 13, 2026 (semafor.com/article/10/13/2026/...): Volta's roughly $5B debt deal for a Norway AI data center, with Anthropic as end customer. JPMorgan and Goldman are marketing it at a yield of at least 11%, anchored by a $1.5B Apollo order. Commitments were due Oct 14, and some investors pushed back. Final pricing is NOT confirmed. (2) Bloomberg (news.bgov.com), Oct 9, 2026: Nvidia-backed Firmus is exploring a $2-3B private round after shelving its roughly $5B Australian IPO on Oct 8. The original Bloomberg piece 'Nvidia-Backed IPO's Cratering Demand Sends Warning on AI Funding' is dated 2026-10-08, one day before the window. (3) Investing.com and FT, as relayed: CreditSights' Jordan Chalfin attributed the CoreWeave selloff to a mismatch between long data-center leases and shorter customer contracts. OUT OF WINDOW, do not present as new: CoreWeave's $3.5B euro/dollar junk bond (about June 2026); Lambda's $1.008B delayed-draw loan (Oct 1); the Meta-linked $12B Texas data-center bond (late Sept, Reuters via Daily Caller). items.safe_wording: StockStory (Oct 13) tied the storage-stock drop to China's CXMT announcing denser DDR5 server-memory plans, which prompted a reassessment of tight memory supply. CNBC (Oct 13) reported memory-linked names falling for a second day. On Oct 14, TradingKey's market wrap grouped Seagate and Western Digital with memory stocks that fell after the hotter-than-expected September CPI revived Fed rate-hike bets. As background, an Oct 2 Nikkei report said Toshiba plans to double HDD capacity. CXMT makes DRAM, not hard drives, so label the read-through as group selling or sentiment rather than a direct competitive hit. Mention the UBS cut only as 'Benzinga cited a UBS price-target cut', without the $470 figure or a date.
